newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Ed nuke seen restarting next week.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Ed nuke seen restarting next week.

text.p: Detroit Edison's 1,116 megawatt Fermi 2 nuclear power plant is expected to restart next week and return to the grid several days later, about a week later than originally scheduled, the company said Thursday.
"The restart has been delayed while we're working to resolve an electrical problem with one of four emergency diesel generators," said company spokesman Scott Simons.
The Monroe County, Mich., unit was shut Sept 27 for scheduled refueling and maintenance, and was slated to return to service Nov 18.
Fermi 2 accounts for 11 percent of Detroit Edison's installed generation capacity and up to 16 percent of its daily electricity output.
Detroit Edison is a subsidiary of DTE Energy Co.
